run_note: Monday 2026-08-17, 15:45Z, first US session in three days. ONE LEAD ITEM AND IT IS A FLEET-WIDE FREEZE, not a single bot. Every one of the nine paper books stopped writing state at 2026-08-17T12:18:2xZ and has been dark for 3h27m against a 13.4-minute cadence — roughly 15 missed cycles — which means the fleet went blind 72 minutes BEFORE the 13:30Z open and has not marked, decided or traded through the first two hours of the session. This is NOT the staleness pattern the check was written for (one bot stale against a healthy fleet); it is the whole fleet stale against a healthy VPS. The job is alive: run 32026664913 started 12:31:34Z, its 'Trade loop' step began 12:32:04Z and is still in_progress, with ZERO commits and ZERO annotations in 3h13m of running. So the loop is hung mid-cycle, not crashed and not throttled. I can rule out a code regression: the checkout at 12:31:36Z is byte-identical in src/ to the job before it, which ran 26 clean cycles and pushed every one (run 31999127921, 06:37Z-12:31Z, 1 push warning, 0 rebase conflicts — so yesterday's rebase-conflict fault did NOT recur). The structural exposure is visible in bot.yml: the roster loop runs eleven bots serially with no per-bot timeout, so one network call that never returns freezes all eleven and the loop reports nothing. The job's budget expires ~18:20Z, and a run has been queued behind the concurrency lock since 15:03Z, so on current evidence the fleet stays dark for most of the remaining session. I did NOT run any bot locally: unlike the 08-16 hypecrypto case there is no console line to recover, and running them writes state. SECOND ITEM, THE SAME FAULT IN A DIFFERENT COSTUME: a SECOND consecutive overnight cron gap of 6h11m, 00:29Z to 06:40Z. Cause is different from today's hang and different from yesterday's discarded job — the 18:42Z job simply exhausted its 345-minute budget at 00:29Z and GitHub accepted no replacement start until 06:37Z (the 05:47Z run sat queued 50 minutes). That is the throttling hole bot.yml's own comment says no single job can span. 24h cycle coverage is 62.6% (538 dark minutes of 1,440), down from 76.3% yesterday and 87.6% Saturday: THREE CONSECUTIVE DAYS OF DEGRADATION, three different root causes, and the design target is 82%. The VPS lottery loop over the same 24 hours: 255 commits, largest gap 6.5 minutes, no holes. The contrast is the argument for the external trigger. THIRD: hypecrypto is still frozen, now 47.9 hours, and the owner's fix (9f64b5ea, 12:47:42Z, routing spot data through Binance's mirror) landed 16 minutes AFTER the running job checked out, so it cannot take effect until the next job starts. FILL AUDIT PASSES AND IS NON-VACUOUS. The nine paper books executed zero trades (trade-array lengths all unchanged: allweather 14, analyst 1, commodity 3, congress 10, crypto 134, hunter 21, meanrev 7, scholar 1, sentiment 28) — though today that is an outage, not restraint. The real-money lottery book put through 6 fills across 3 round trips; all 6 verified inside Binance mainnet 1-minute ranges within +/-5 minutes of their recorded timestamps, plus the 08-16 CHIP exit that closed after my last run. All USDT pairs, so the market-hours gate does not apply. No SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT. The method reproduces every 08-14 mark to the cent (allweather validated exactly at 1018.60), and I have labelled every reconstructed number as reconstructed in its attribution line rather than passing it off as a bot mark. On that basis the nine books are worth 9,662.54 live against 9,674.89 recorded, so the dashboards are currently overstating the fleet by 12.35 and will keep drifting until the loop restarts. The day is a software-down/semis-up rotation (IGV -1.42% vs SMH +2.01%) on a flat index (SPY -0.10%): congress owns both sides and lost 6.45, meanrev lost 20.67 on a UNH move I could not find a cause for and logged 'unknown', commodity made 10.03 on broad commodity strength. THE LOTTERY BOOK LOST MONEY THREE TIMES OUT OF THREE, -0.79 realized on a ~$39 base, and the CHIP whipsaw I opened yesterday ran a THIRD time: the LATE guard refused CHIP at 09:10Z and 09:16Z, passed it at 09:21Z, and the fade rule cut it 86 minutes later at 0.02996 — CHIP now trades 0.03010, ABOVE that exit, so today the cut was the losing side of the same contradiction. It also bought LTC, a top-10 major, off a hype screen. MY OWN SCORING WAS A BAD DAY AND I AM NOT SOFTENING IT: two directional losses, one noise-level win, one neutral I refuse to bank. Both congress calls were wrong in the same way — I argued name-specific credit and earnings damage would keep bleeding, and both names simply went up with a sector rally.
